subject.title: Workspace symlinks to ~/.openclaw subdirectories are rejected by boundary path check

question: Should fixed workspace bootstrap files be allowed to follow symlinks from the workspace into `~/.openclaw` sibling directories, and which `~/.openclaw` roots must remain blocked from prompt injection?
rationale: The failure is source-reproducible, but the fix changes which local files can become startup prompt authority, so automation cannot safely choose the filesystem trust boundary.

options.title: Narrow bootstrap-only exception
options.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap filenames to follow symlinks to maintainer-approved shared roots while denying private OpenClaw state, credentials, sessions, caches, logs, non-regular files, hardlinks, dangling symlinks, and oversized files.

options.title: Keep strict boundary with diagnostics
options.body: Continue rejecting external symlink targets but render boundary-blocked bootstrap files distinctly from missing files so users can diagnose the setup without weakening the boundary.

options.title: Require explicit trusted-path config
options.body: Add or reuse an operator-controlled allowlist before external bootstrap symlinks can be read, accepting the extra config and upgrade-documentation surface.

recommendation.title: Narrow bootstrap-only exception
recommendation.body: Allow only fixed bootstrap filenames to follow symlinks to maintainer-approved shared roots while denying private OpenClaw state, credentials, sessions, caches, logs, non-regular files, hardlinks, dangling symlinks, and oversized files.
